c.tagline: Colorful island town on Lake Peten Itza and Guatemala's gateway to the Maya ruins of Tikal.

taxi.fareNote: There are no ride-hailing apps in Peten. Short hops around Flores island and Santa Elena are by tuk-tuk (mototaxi) for a few quetzales; longer trips and airport runs are by taxi or hotel shuttle at a fixed price agreed in advance.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the PNC (national police); 122 the volunteer firefighters (bomberos) who also run ambulances; 1500 the municipal firefighters and 1554 the Red Cross. Peten is remote, so hotels and tour operators are often the fastest source of help.

hood_landmark.Cerro / El Remate: El Remate, Lake Peten Itza, Guatemala

avoid.reason: Avoid the back streets of Santa Elena, across the causeway, after dark — petty crime is more common there than on Flores island.
Watch bags at the Santa Elena bus terminal and vet tour/shuttle operators to avoid overcharging scams.

hood_desc: The colorful little island old town on Lake Peten Itza, a grid of pastel houses, cobbled lanes, lakeside restaurants and hostels crowned by the twin-domed cathedral; fully walkable and the atmospheric base most travelers choose for visiting Tikal.

The bustling mainland town across the causeway, home to the airport, bus terminal, banks and markets; less charming but cheaper and convenient, with lakefront hotels and the main transport connections.

The workaday town just west of Santa Elena, the largest and most local of the three, with budget lodging and a couple of lakeshore boutique hotels; quiet and residential, a short tuk-tuk from the island.

A tranquil lakeside village about 30 km northeast toward Tikal, strung along the shore of Lake Peten Itza with swimming spots, jungle lodges and sunset views; a peaceful, nature-focused alternative to the island.

The great Maya city and national park an hour north, where towering limestone temples rise above the rainforest canopy amid howler monkeys and toucans; a cluster of on-site jungle lodges lets you catch sunrise and sunset over the ruins.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water only.

transit.hours: Tuk-tuks run through the day and into the evening; boats and shuttles run on demand or at set departure times arranged the day before.
transit.note: There is no formal public bus network on the island; the flat little town is walkable, tuk-tuks handle Santa Elena and the causeway, lanchas cross the lake to San Andres/San Jose and lakeside lodges, and shuttle vans run the 1-1.5 hr road to Tikal.
transit.pay: Tuk-tuks around Flores island and Santa Elena charge a few quetzales per ride, paid in cash; lake boats (lanchas) and tourist shuttles to Tikal, Yaxha or the border are booked and paid in cash through hotels and agencies.

bus: Terminal Nueva Santa Elena (intercity coaches: Fuente del Norte, ADN, Linea Dorada)
Tourist shuttle vans to Tikal, Yaxha, Belize and Rio Dulce
ferry: Lake Peten Itza passenger lanchas (to San Andres, San Jose, lakeside lodges)

transit.m: Taxi or tuk-tuk to Flores island, ~10-15 min
Hotel shuttle to Santa Elena / Flores when arranged

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants (sometimes already added as 'propina'); small tips for guides, drivers and boatmen are appreciated.
